title: Border and Protocol
premise: Lena Marchetti, a veteran interpreter embedded with a faltering peace delegation in a contested border city, receives calls on an unregistered burner phone from her former handler—the man who trained her and whom she buried fifteen years ago. The voice reveals that the delegation is a decoy for an intelligence operation that will sacrifice everyone at the table, including Lena, to justify a war. Torn between the duty that gave her a place in the world and the people she's come to love within the delegation, Lena races to expose and dismantle the network before the summit collapses on schedule. In the end she burns her own legend, testifies at cost of everything, and walks away stateless but free, choosing connection over protocol.
about_author: Mara Amberdale is the pen name of a former NGO field coordinator who spent a decade working along contested borders in Eastern Europe. She writes thrillers about the quiet people who translate between worlds that would rather destroy each other.

chapters.title: The Language of Waiting
chapters.summary: POV Lena. The peace delegation arrives in the border city of Vessengrad amid stalemate; Lena interprets a hostile first session, establishing her competence and careful invisibility. She notices a colleague, Tomas, watching her too closely. Emotional beat: weary belonging—she has found a fragile home inside rules.

chapters.title: A Number That Should Not Exist
chapters.summary: POV Lena. A burner phone hidden in her hotel Bible rings; the voice belongs to Anton Reiner, her dead handler. He warns the delegation is bait and gives her forty-eight hours to verify it herself. Emotional beat: vertigo—the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Flashback-heavy chapter, POV Lena. We learn of her recruitment as a young interpreter, the training program called the Chancery, and how she faked Reiner's death to escape it. Emotional beat: grief reframed—her survival was built on a betrayal she never finished understanding.

chapters.title: Coffee with a Ghost
chapters.summary: POV Lena. She tests Reiner's claim by checking delegation logistics and finds a sealed annex no one will explain. Tomas offers her coffee and unexpected warmth; she lies to him fluently and hates how easy it is. Emotional beat: loneliness sharpened by intimacy.

chapters.title: The Annex
chapters.summary: POV Lena. Using interpreter access, she photographs the annex: troop movement schedules disguised as security protocols. Reiner confirms—the summit's failure is scheduled, its casualties pre-counted. Emotional beat: cold clarity replacing denial.

chapters.title: Rules of Engagement
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. Tomas, actually a Chancery watcher assigned to monitor Lena, reports her anomalies to his superior while concealing his growing attachment. Emotional beat: divided loyalty—he begins editing his own reports.

chapters.title: Dead Drop in the Old Market
chapters.summary: POV Lena. She meets Reiner face-to-face in a crowded market; he looks older than memory allows. He explains the network's structure and asks her to help burn it, offering nothing but truth. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance with the man who made her.

chapters.title: What the Interpreter Heard
chapters.summary: POV Lena. During a plenary session, Lena deliberately mistranslates a delegate's threat to buy time, committing her first open act of sabotage. A Chancery listener notices the deviation. Emotional beat: exhilaration curdling into fear.

chapters.title: The Listener
chapters.summary: POV antagonist, Deputy Director Ilse Varga of the Chancery. Varga reviews the mistranslation, recognizes Lena's signature style, and activates a termination protocol disguised as a promotion. Emotional beat: bureaucratic menace—evil as paperwork.

chapters.title: Promotion
chapters.summary: POV Lena. Lena is offered transfer to the 'secure secretariat'—a gilded trap. Reiner tells her accepting means dying quietly after the summit; refusing means dying loudly now. Emotional beat: the price of survival itemized.

chapters.title: Tomas Breaks Protocol
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. Ordered to plant surveillance in Lena's room, Tomas instead warns her obliquely through a translated phrase only she would catch. Emotional beat: love choosing sides against duty.

chapters.title: Two Truths in One Bed
chapters.summary: POV alternating Lena/Tomas. They confess partially—she admits she's being hunted, he admits he was sent to watch her—and choose each other anyway, pooling what they know. Emotional beat: vulnerability as strategy and grace.

chapters.title: The Network Map
chapters.summary: POV Lena. Combining Reiner's knowledge, Tomas's files, and her own archives, they map the Chancery's chain: Varga, three ministers, and a general who profits from the war the failed summit will ignite. Emotional beat: the enemy acquires faces.

chapters.title: Reiner's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Reiner. Reiner admits he let Lena believe she killed him to sever her ties cleanly—a final act of tradecraft that destroyed them both. He asks forgiveness without expecting it. Emotional beat: the trainer unmade by his own methods.

chapters.title: Countermove
chapters.summary: POV Varga. Varga feeds false evidence framing Lena as a foreign agent, turning the delegation's own security chief against her. Warrants are drafted. Emotional beat: the trap closing with polite efficiency.

chapters.title: Forty Minutes in the Dark
chapters.summary: POV Lena. Detained briefly during a power cut staged by the Chancery, Lena escapes using skills she swore off, killing no one but leaving a trail she can't erase. Emotional beat: survival costing innocence again.

chapters.title: The General's Table
chapters.summary: POV Lena. At a banquet, Lena records the general and a minister confirming the summit-failure timeline, then passes the recording to a journalist via Tomas. Emotional beat: courage as translation—turning secrets into public language.

chapters.title: Everything Burns on Schedule
chapters.summary: POV multiple. The Chancery detonates its plan early: an attack on the delegation hall. Reiner dies shielding Lena, his death finally real. Emotional beat: climax—grief, chaos, and resolve fused.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Lena. With the hall burning and communications jammed, Lena uses the interpreter booth's live feed to broadcast the recording and the network map in three languages. Emotional beat: her voice, finally her own weapon.

chapters.title: Varga's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Varga. Exposed mid-operation, Varga attempts to erase evidence and escape; Tomas intercepts her at the airfield, trading his career for her capture. Emotional beat: duty redeemed by choice.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: POV Lena. Weeks later, Lena testifies before an international commission, surrendering her cover identities and legal existence to do so. The Chancery's leadership falls; she becomes officially no one. Emotional beat: the price paid in full, without regret.

chapters.title: Border and Protocol
chapters.summary: POV Lena. Stateless but free, Lena stands at an ordinary border crossing with Tomas, no credentials, no handler, no legend. Asked her profession, she answers simply: 'Interpreter.' Emotional beat: belonging redefined—not granted by institutions, but chosen.
